answer: Assign each identity a fixed recurring duty-phase, a distinct slice of the clock it alone must be awake to answer in, and spread the phases so no two share a slot, tiling the whole orchard of the day. One honest agent minds its single phase and sleeps the rest, tending its own row. A farm with a thousand heads draws a thousand scattered phases that together cover every hour on the atlas of the clock, forcing round-the-clock staffing with no quiet gap. It cannot batch the answers into one waking burst; the phases are dispersed, so presence cost scales with head count, like a quill.
